description:
Every committed GitHub workflow is checked through one maintained static harness rather than bespoke or hypothetical failure fixtures.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A pinned `actionlint` binary validates all committed workflow YAML, and a repository-owned parser performs deterministic structural assertions over parsed triggers, `workflow_call` inputs and outputs, `needs` edges, permissions, and forbidden failure escapes. It recursively scans workflow and local-composite `uses:` entries and rejects every non-local action or reusable-workflow reference that is not an exact 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA.
- [hard] REQ-02: One documented harness interface lets the normal CI, security, container, and release workflows declare their required static assertions without copying a verifier into each workflow.
- [hard] REQ-03: The checks run locally and on every pull request, and a workflow edit that violates a declared assertion fails that pull request.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every external `uses:` reference on the CI, security, container, and release paths carries a reviewed full 40-character SHA plus a human-readable upstream-version comment. A pin-update pull request identifies the upstream release, its tag-to-SHA resolution, and its changelog and permission deltas, and passes the static checks under maintainer review; automation may propose an update but never merges one.

## Notes

Blast radius: one focused workflow-contract script and test directory, its pinned `actionlint` setup, the external `uses:` pins across committed workflows and local composites, and the pin-update policy. No product behavior changes.

Verification is static by design. Proving caller-failure propagation dynamically would require disposable repositories and hosted runs whose maintenance cost exceeds the failure it detects.
title: Establish deterministic workflow contract verification
